title: General constructible internal Hom and finite coefficient change
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, with $q$ a power of $p$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and integers $n\geq m\geq1$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ and $B=A_{E,m}$, and use the quotient homomorphism $A\to B$. Work on either small site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ or $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with constant coefficient ring sheaves. Here $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ means bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude over $A$: there is a finite interval outside which $K\otimes_A^L F$ has zero cohomology for every sheaf $F$ of $A$-modules in degree zero. Write $T_B=T\otimes_A^L B$ for derived coefficient change, and $H_A(K,M)=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)$ for derived internal Hom.

For every $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the map
$$
v^{A,B}_{K,M}:H_A(K,M)\otimes_A^L B\longrightarrow H_B(K_B,M_B)
$$
is an isomorphism in $D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$. It is the unique transpose of coefficient change of the evaluation $H_A(K,M)\otimes_A^L K\to M$, under the canonical tensor comparison. It is natural in both variables and respects evaluation, tensor–Hom adjunction, and composition of internal-Hom morphisms. For $1\leq r\leq m$ and $C=A_{E,r}$ it satisfies
$$
v^{A,C}_{K,M}=v^{B,C}_{K_B,M_B}\circ\bigl(v^{A,B}_{K,M}\otimes_B^L C\bigr),
$$
using the canonical identifications of successive derived scalar extensions. These assertions hold for both finite coefficient sites, with their canonical site-comparison maps.

proof.text: Every finite-type $k$-scheme used here is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (the only ideals of the field are zero and the whole ring). First work on the small etale site. Put $F_{A,B}(T)=T\otimes_A^L B$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] this is an exact functor on the ambient derived categories, even when $B$ is not flat over $A$. For $T\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, choose a bounded flat constructible model $P$ by the etale constructible variant of [lem-sf-flat-model]. The bounded flat complex is K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria], and [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] shows that $P\otimes_A B$ is a K-flat complex of flat $B$-sheaves representing $F_{A,B}T$. Each of its finitely many terms is constructible: on a partition trivializing $P^i$ with finite module value $V$, its tensor is constant with value $V\otimes_A B$, which is finite since both rings and $V$ are finite. Thus [lem-sf-flat-model], now over $B$, gives $T_B\in D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$ with the same Tor interval. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity of the underlying topos with ring map $A\to B$ to obtain the canonical tensor comparison. On K-flat models it reassociates pure tensors, so it preserves tensor associativity. For later use, the same theorem for a morphism of small etale topoi with constant coefficients takes bounded flat models to bounded flat models in the same degrees. Inverse image is exact by [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and preserves constructibility: pull back a finite locally closed partition and its finite locally constant trivializations. Thus etale pullback preserves bounded constructibility and the Tor interval. Its compatibility with coefficient change is the termwise reassociation of these same tensor models.

proof.text: The tensor–Hom adjunction used throughout is obtained as follows. Choose flat K-flat representatives for $T,K$ and a K-injective representative $I$ for $M$. By [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,I)$ is K-injective. The total tensor of the two K-flat representatives is K-flat: tensoring it with an acyclic complex is the iterated tensor, first acyclic by K-flatness of $K$ and then by K-flatness of $T$. The functorial complex isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] identifies $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(T,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,I))$ with $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes K),I)$. Taking zeroth global cohomology and applying [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] gives the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(T,H_A(K,M))=\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes_A^L K,M)$, with the usual evaluation and transpose. For $H=H_A(K,M)$ define $v_{K,M}^{A,B}$ as the transpose of $F_{A,B}H\otimes_B^L K_B\cong F_{A,B}(H\otimes_A^L K)\xrightarrow{F_{A,B}(\mathrm{ev}_A)}M_B$, using the tensor comparison established in step 1. Choose a nonnegative integer $d_X$ bounding $\dim X$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], taking $d_X=0$ when $X$ is empty. Apply [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] over $A$ and over $B$, and step 1, to see that both the source and the target lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$. This also defines the same comparison for all ambient pairs, without a finiteness assertion on their internal Hom.

proof.text:
Fix $M$. Consider the full class $\mathcal C_M$ of $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ for which this particular $v_{K,M}^{A,B}$ is invertible. Internal Hom is contravariantly exact by [lem-sf-hom-triangulated]; coefficient change is exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The evaluation transpose commutes with shifts and cone triangles: on the Hom/tensor complex models of step 2 its components are the evaluation chain maps, with the usual shifted differentials, so the squares with the shifted connecting map commute as well. Thus the comparisons form a morphism of the resulting distinguished triangles. The two-out-of-three assertion [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $\mathcal C_M$ closed under triangles and shifts. It contains zero, and is closed under summands: naturality at a splitting makes the comparison block diagonal, and the corresponding diagonal blocks of its inverse invert the two blocks.

Here is the generation argument on the etale site itself. Let $\mathcal G_X$ be the thick subcategory generated by $Rg_*j_!L$, where $s=g\circ j:S\hookrightarrow X$, $j:S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ is open, $g:\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ is closed, and $L$ is finite lisse with flat stalks. These are in $D^b_{ctf}$: their constructibility follows from their finite lisse strata, and the etale open tensor formula proved in step 8 and [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], together with exact $j_!$ and exact closed pushforward in [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement], show Tor interval $[0,0]$ by tensoring against an arbitrary degree-zero ambient module sheaf. For any $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, [lem-sf-flat-model] gives a bounded complex of flat constructible sheaves $P$. Its finite stupid-truncation triangles reduce $K\in\mathcal G_X$ to its terms $F=P^q$.

Induct on the finite dimension of the ambient scheme to show that every such $F$ lies in $\mathcal G_X$, with the empty scheme as base case. By [fin2-lem-lisse-dense-open] there is an open $j_U:U\hookrightarrow X$ on which $F|_U$ is lisse and whose closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ has smaller dimension. Both restrictions have Tor interval $[0,0]$ and remain constructible by the etale pullback argument of step 1; they are degree-zero sheaves since constant-coefficient inverse image is exact. Apply [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] to obtain $j_{U!}F|_U\to F\to i_*i^*F\to$. The first term is a generator. The induction hypothesis expresses $i^*F$ through flat-lisse locally closed generators on $Z$. Exact $i_*$ carries those triangles and summands to triangles and summands on $X$, and carries a generator $Rg'_*j'_!L$ to $R(ig')_*j'_!L$: the closed pushforwards are exact and compose by their sectionwise definition, and the closure of the stratum in $X$ lies in $Z$. Thus $i_*i^*F\in\mathcal G_X$, whence $F\in\mathcal G_X$. This proves the required etale generation directly on the chosen site. It suffices to prove invertibility for $K=Rg_*j_!L=Rs_!L$.

proof.text: The generator sheaf $L$ is site-perfect, not merely stalkwise perfect. Indeed lisseness supplies an actual etale covering on which $L$ is constant with finite $A$-module value $V$. Its flat stalks say that $V[0]$ has Tor interval $[0,0]$. The finite local ring $A$ is Noetherian (its set of ideals is finite), so [lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect] applied to $V[0]$ gives a finite projective module in degree zero, free because $A$ is local. Pulling this model back as a constant sheaf on that covering is the required site-perfect model. In particular $L$ is bounded constructible of Tor interval $[0,0]$. The etale finite-free calculation in step 6 will therefore apply to $L$.

proof.text: Set $N=Rs_A^!M$. To check its domain, factor $s=g\circ j$ with $g:\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ closed and $j:S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ open, so $Rs_A^!=j^*Rg_A^!$. Choose a nonnegative integer $d\geq\dim X$, possible by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], taking $d=0$ if $X$ is empty. The complement of $g$ is quasi-compact since $X$ is Noetherian. The field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ is separably closed, $A=A_{E,n}$ is a finite ring annihilated by a power of $\ell\neq p$, and the ambient scheme is the finite-type scheme $X$ of dimension at most $d$. Thus the general quasi-compact-open clause of the current [thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional] supplies both vanishing above $2d$ for all sheaves and constructibility of all higher direct images of constructible sheaves. No affine-chart specialization or nonemptiness of a chart is used. Thus [prop-exc-closed-tor] applies with $c=2d$: if $M$ has Tor interval $[a,b]$, $Rg_A^!M$ is bounded constructible with Tor interval $[a,b+2d+1]$. Its open pullback remains finite-Tor constructible by the etale pullback argument of step 1. Consequently $N\in D^b_{ctf}(S,A)$. This preservation is not a conclusion of the coefficient-comparison lemma.

proof.text: Put $Q=H_A(L,N)$. The stratum $S$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Choose a nonnegative dimension bound $d_S$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], with $d_S=0$ for the empty stratum. Apply [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] on $S$, with the same finite coefficient ring $A$, to the two finite-Tor constructible arguments just obtained; it gives $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(S,A)$. Here is the required etale coefficient comparison directly. Internal Hom restricts to every etale covering object by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. On the cover of step 4 write $L=A^{r}[0]$ and choose a bounded flat model $P$ for $N$ using [lem-sf-flat-model]. The ringed-site Hom model [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] identifies $H_A(L,N)$ with $P^{\oplus r}$, and the $B$-coefficient Hom with $(P\otimes_A B)^{\oplus r}$. The evaluation-defined comparison is the identity between these models, including for $r=0$. Its cone therefore restricts to zero on a cover; equivalently its cohomology has zero geometric stalks, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes it an isomorphism globally. We have the isomorphism $Q_B\xrightarrow{v_{L,N}^{A,B}}H_B(L_B,N_B)$, preserving evaluation. Only this local finite-free calculation, not the theorem being proved for arbitrary $K$, is used here.

proof.text:
Use the canonical etale internal adjunction [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] for $s=g\circ j$, a compactifiable locally closed immersion between Noetherian schemes. In the factorization of step 5, $Rs_!=Rg_*j_!$ since $g$ is closed and hence proper. The formula $Rs_!=Rg_*j_!$ is the chosen-compactification definition [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. The sheaf adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ is [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], and $j_!$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]; $j^*$ is exact inverse image as specified in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Apply their unit and counit degreewise to complexes. Their triangle identities still hold degreewise, and both functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms, so these transformations descend and satisfy the triangle identities on derived categories. Thus $j_!\dashv j^*$ also there. Together with the closed exceptional adjunction used in step 5, the right adjoint of $Rg_*j_!$ is $j^*Rg_A^!$: explicitly,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Rg_*j_!P,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!P,Rg_A^!M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,j^*Rg_A^!M).$$
Thus the right adjoint $s^\times$ in that theorem identifies canonically with the $Rs_A^!$ of step 5, including its counit. We obtain the following composite of isomorphisms:
$$
\begin{aligned}
F_{A,B}H_A(Rs_{!,A}L,M)&\cong F_{A,B}Rs_{*,A}Q\\
&\xrightarrow{c_{s,Q}}Rs_{*,B}(Q_B)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rs_*v_{L,N}}Rs_{*,B}H_B(L_B,N_B)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rs_*H_B(1,b_{s,M})}Rs_{*,B}H_B(L_B,Rs_B^!M_B)\\
&\cong H_B(Rs_{!,B}L_B,M_B).
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $c_{s,Q}$ is [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], with its finite-Tor hypothesis checked in step 6. We construct the required $b_{s,M}$ on the etale site, without using the pro-etale closed-shriek statement.

First construct it for the closed factor $g:\overline S\hookrightarrow X$. Put $N_g=Rg_A^!M$ and let $t:V=X\setminus\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ be the complementary open. The exceptional adjunction exists on the etale ambient categories by [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. The etale closed-support triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] is
$$g_*N_g\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{g,A}}M\xrightarrow{\eta_t}Rt_*t^*M\longrightarrow g_*N_g[1].$$
Its analogue over $B$ applies to $M_B$. Step 5 gives the finite-Tor constructibility of $N_g$, and the etale pullback argument of step 1 gives it for $t^*M$. Thus [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] gives both $c_{g,N_g}$ and $c_{t,t^*M}$ as isomorphisms. After the pullback/coefficient identification, the latter satisfies $c_{t,t^*M}\circ F_X(\eta_{t,M})=\eta_{t,M_B}$: transpose under $t^*\dashv Rt_*$, use its defining counit transpose, and both transposes are $1_{t^*M_B}$ by the adjunction triangle identity. Apply the exact $F_X$ to the displayed support triangle and compare it to the support triangle for $M_B$. The maps on the middle and right terms are the identity and $c_{t,t^*M}$. Rotate once and apply (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to complete these maps to a morphism of triangles. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] its remaining map is an isomorphism. Under $c_{g,N_g}$ it is a map
$$\delta:g_*((N_g)_B)\xrightarrow{\sim}g_*Rg_B^!M_B,\qquad
\epsilon_{g,B}\circ\delta=F_X(\epsilon_{g,A})\circ c_{g,N_g}^{-1}.$$

For completeness the needed full faithfulness is on the etale derived categories as well. [lem-kun-04ca] gives full faithfulness and $g^*g_*\cong1$ for abelian sheaves. A module action consists of scalar endomorphisms satisfying the ring relations, so full faithfulness uniquely transports these endomorphisms and their relations; the same assertions hold for constant-$B$ module sheaves. Both functors are exact, by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] for $g_*$ and [def-kun-projection-formula-map] for $g^*$. Their degreewise adjunction and counit descend through quasi-isomorphisms, with $g^*g_*\cong1$. Hence $g_*$ is fully faithful on the derived categories, and conservative since $g^*g_*\cong1$. Let $b_{g,M}$ be the transpose under $g_*\dashv Rg_B^!$ of $F_X(\epsilon_{g,A})c_{g,N_g}^{-1}$. The adjunction and full faithfulness say that composition with $\epsilon_{g,B}$ bijects maps $g_*P\to g_*Rg_B^!M_B$ with maps $g_*P\to M_B$. Therefore $g_*b_{g,M}=\delta$, independently of the chosen triangle completion. Conservativity makes $b_{g,M}$ invertible. This definition also gives its naturality and exceptional-counit equality directly.

Set $b_{s,M}=j^*b_{g,M}$ after the canonical pullback/coefficient identification, so its source is $(j^*N_g)_B$ and its target is $j^*Rg_B^!M_B=Rs_B^!M_B$. It is invertible. The counit of $g_*j_!\dashv j^*Rg^!$ is $\epsilon_g\circ g_*(\epsilon_j)$; use the equality just proved for $g$ together with the following explicit open comparison. the independent open tensor calculation at the start of step 8, with $T=B$, gives $Fj_!P\cong j_!F P$ on flat models. Under this comparison the counit $j_!j^*T\to T$ commutes with coefficient change, since its defining section maps are identities on objects factoring through the open, and zero on the other summands, by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. For the closed factor use $c_{g,j_!P}$ of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]; $j_!P$ is finite-Tor constructible by the bounded flat model and the open tensor calculation. Composing these two maps defines the compact-support coefficient comparison for the chosen $s=g j$. Its naturality and compatibility with the closed ordinary counit follow from the stated transpose characterization of $c_g$. These comparisons and the composite-adjunction formula give
$$\epsilon_{s,B}\circ Rs_{!,B}(b_{s,M})=F_X(\epsilon_{s,A})$$
under the compact-support coefficient comparison. Both $s$ and its source are separated of finite type. Finally this explicitly constructed compact-support comparison identifies $F_{A,B}(Rs_{!,A}L)$ with $Rs_{!,B}L_B$.

proof.text:
We must identify the isomorphism of step 7 with $v_{Rs_!L,M}^{A,B}$. First establish the open tensor formula on the etale site. The open adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] gives the natural map $j_!(P\otimes_A j^*T)\to j_!P\otimes_A T$, whose restriction to $U$ is the identity. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar], its geometric stalks are the identity tensor map on $U$ and $0\to0$ off $U$, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes it an isomorphism. In particular $j_!$ preserves flatness, since this formula, exact $j^*$ and exact $j_!$ preserve injections after tensoring with a flat $P$; exactness is [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. It also preserves K-flatness: for an acyclic complex $T$, $j^*T$ is acyclic and the same termwise tensor formula identifies $j_!P\otimes T$ with the acyclic $j_!(P\otimes j^*T)$. Thus applying this termwise formula to flat K-flat models gives the canonical etale derived open projection isomorphism. All its tensor and coefficient identifications restrict to the identity on $U$ and to zero off $U$; equality of such maps follows from the open adjunction. The inverse projection isomorphism for $s_!$ is obtained by composing this open projection isomorphism with the canonical proper projection isomorphism [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] for the closed immersion $g$; its hypotheses hold since $g$ is proper of finite type between the Noetherian schemes of step 1. The first arrow in the following pairing is this projection isomorphism followed by the $s^*\dashv Rs_*$ counit. The canonical internal adjunction [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] is the transpose of the pairing $Rs_*H_A(L,N)\otimes_A^L Rs_!L\to Rs_!(H_A(L,N)\otimes_A^L L)\xrightarrow{Rs_!\mathrm{ev}}Rs_!N\xrightarrow{\epsilon_s}M$. Transpose the composite of step 7 and evaluate it on $Rs_{!,B}L_B$. Write $\alpha_A:s^*Rs_{*,A}Q\to Q$ for the ordinary adjunction counit, and put $F_X=F_{A,B}$ on $X$ and $F_S=F_{A,B}$ on $S$. The projection morphism is defined as the transpose of the ordinary counit tensored with the identity in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. For the coefficient object $B$, this is the canonical coefficient projection $c_{s,Q}$ of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], with $B$ acting on the $B$ factor on both sides. Its defining transpose therefore gives
$$\alpha_B\circ s^*c_{s,Q}=F_S(\alpha_A)$$
after $s^*F_X\cong F_Ss^*$. This is the equality needed for the first arrow of the pairing; the projection isomorphisms commute with coefficient change because their adjoints are these counits, and the tensor and pullback identifications of step 1 and the compact-support comparison of step 7 preserve those counits. Next, the finite-free Hom comparison of step 6 carries the middle evaluation to its coefficient change; and the etale construction in step 7 identifies $\epsilon_{s,B}\circ Rs_{!,B}(b_{s,M})$ with the coefficient change of $\epsilon_{s,A}$ under the compact-support comparison. Substituting these three equalities leaves exactly $F_{A,B}$ of the displayed pairing, with only the canonical reassociations of tensor established in step 1. Its transpose is the map of step 2. Thus $v$ itself, rather than just some isomorphism between its endpoints, is invertible on every generator.

proof.text: Step 8 puts every flat-lisse locally closed generator of the etale construction in step 3 in $\mathcal C_M$. Its triangle and summand closure, applied first through the dimension induction for each flat constructible sheaf and then through the finite stupid-truncation triangles of a flat constructible model, gives $\mathcal C_M=D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Since $M$ was any finite-Tor constructible complex, the specified comparison is an isomorphism for every pair in the statement.

proof.text: The evaluation identity is, by construction, $\mathrm{ev}_B\circ(v_{K,M}^{A,B}\otimes1)=F_{A,B}(\mathrm{ev}_A)$ after the tensor comparison. For a morphism $u:T\otimes_A^L K\to M$ with transpose $u^\sharp:T\to H_A(K,M)$, uncurrying $v_{K,M}^{A,B}\circ F_{A,B}(u^\sharp)$ gives $F_{A,B}(u)$, by this identity and naturality. Uniqueness in tensor–Hom adjunction proves preservation of transposes. For $f:K'\to K$, compare $v_{K',M}F_{A,B}(H_A(f,1))$ and $H_B(f_B,1)v_{K,M}$. Their transposes, with source $F_{A,B}H_A(K,M)\otimes_B^L K'_B$, are both $F_{A,B}(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}\circ(1\otimes f))$. For $g:M\to M'$, compare $v_{K,M'}F_{A,B}(H_A(1,g))$ and $H_B(1,g_B)v_{K,M}$. Their transposes are both $F_{A,B}(g\circ\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})$. Uniqueness of transpose gives both naturality equations.

proof.text: Write $\mu_A:H_A(M,N)\otimes_A^L H_A(K,M)\to H_A(K,N)$ for internal-Hom composition, characterized by evaluating first at $K$ and then at $M$. To compare $v_{K,N}F_{A,B}(\mu_A)$ with $\mu_B(v_{M,N}\otimes v_{K,M})$, tensor both maps with $K_B$ and evaluate at $N_B$. By the evaluation identity of step 10, both composites are $F_{A,B}$ of the successive evaluations $H_A(M,N)\otimes H_A(K,M)\otimes K\to H_A(M,N)\otimes M\to N$. Tensor associativity and uniqueness of transpose give the composition identity.

proof.text: Let $C=A_{E,r}$ with $1\leq r\leq m$. Compare the direct coefficient map $v^{A,C}_{K,M}$ with $v^{B,C}_{K_B,M_B}\circ F_{B,C}(v^{A,B}_{K,M})$. After tensoring with $K_C$ and evaluating, the first map yields $F_{A,C}(\mathrm{ev}_A)$; the second yields $F_{B,C}F_{A,B}(\mathrm{ev}_A)$ by applying step 10 twice. These agree under the associative identification $(T\otimes_A^L B)\otimes_B^L C\cong T\otimes_A^L C$. The K-flat tensor identifications in step 1 give precisely these identifications: both send a pure tensor $(t\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $t\otimes bc$. Uniqueness of transpose proves the displayed quotient cocycle. For $m=n$, both $v^{A,A}_{K,M}$ and the identity of $H_A(K,M)$ have transpose $\mathrm{ev}_A$, since $F_{A,A}$ and its tensor comparison are the identity under the unit scalar-extension identifications. Uniqueness of transpose gives $v^{A,A}_{K,M}=1$.

proof.text:
For passage to the pro-etale site, $
u_X^*$ is an exact module inverse image by [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] and comes from the geometric morphism of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The ringed-topos tensor-pullback theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] supplies its natural derived tensor comparison. Flat sheaves remain flat by [lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat]. Thus the flat models in [lem-sf-flat-model] are pulled back to flat models. Termwise, inverse image identifies the constant $B$ sheaf with the constant $B$ sheaf and takes $P^i\otimes_A B$ to $(
u_X^*P^i)\otimes_A B$ by the tensor comparison; the $B$ action in both expressions is on that same factor. Consequently $
u_X^*(T\otimes_A^L B)\cong(
u_X^*T)\otimes_A^L B$ as $B$-complexes, not merely after forgetting the $B$ action. On the tensor total complexes all these maps rebracket the same pure tensors, so their identifications agree with tensor associativity. This checks the coefficient and tensor identifications required for site transport.

proof.text:
Every bounded constructible pro-etale pair is $
u_X^*K',
u_X^*M'$ for bounded constructible etale complexes by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. If the original pair has finite Tor amplitude, clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] says that $K',M'$ do also. Apply [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] over $A$ to $K',M'$ and over $B$ to $K'_B,M'_B$; its hypotheses hold by step 1. Its current statement applies at the same finite stages $A_{E,n}$ and $A_{E,m}$ and supplies the canonical evaluation-defined comparison for these finite-Tor first and bounded constructible second variables. These identify the two internal Homs with their pro-etale realizations and identify their evaluations. No dualizing-object or ambient pro-etale exceptional-adjoint assertion is needed here. Together with step 13, they identify the pro-etale $v$ with $
